clue.text: Kentish Town revolutionary occupying list

indicators.note: the revolutionary sits inside, taking up room within the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty
Che Guevara, the crossword's standard revolutionary

explanation.surface: A radical takes over a roll-call in Kentish Town, the north London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kentish Town' looks like the London district, but it means a town in the county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the cathedral city of Rochester lies in the county of Kent.

clue.text: German knight turns up for Italian dish

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name
Sir is a knight's title

explanation.surface: A German knight is served an Italian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice dish cooked slowly in stock, a staple of northern Italian cooking.

clue.text: Name outstanding witch he painted

indicators.note: read as out-standing: the name stands outside the witch, holding it

parts.note: to call is to name
a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: Someone names the outstanding witch that a man painted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise but is read as out-standing: the name stands outside the witch.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was the Russian-French artist, so a painter fits 'he painted'.

clue.text: In doubling possible price, agent finally quits

indicators.note: the last letter of agent goes inside the doubled odds
doubling means the price is written twice in a row

parts.note: evens is a betting price, odds of one to one

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of agent

explanation.surface: A bookie's agent quits after the odds he might offer are doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubling' gives EVENSEVENS; T, the last letter of 'agent', goes between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means owing nothing either way, the level state the idiom describes.

clue.text: Dog kennels appreciative, volunteer starts work

indicators.note: to kennel is to house, so the dog's word holds the other letters

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail them

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A dog's shelter thanks a volunteer who has started work there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kennels' is a verb here: TRAIL houses AV, the starts of 'appreciative' and 'volunteer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is hard, painful labour, a literary synonym for toil.

clue.text: Fancy things beginning to improve in the serving up of a drink

indicators.note: the starting letter of improve is placed within the other letters
in a down entry, served up means written upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lager is a drink

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of improve

explanation.surface: Fancy touches improve the way a drink is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving up' turns A LAGER into REGALA; I from 'improve' goes in to give REGALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are ornate emblems and finery, fancy items worn on state occasions.

clue.text: Currency trickled into Liverpool, perhaps?

indicators.note: into puts the flowing word inside the club's letters

parts.note: Liverpool is an example of a football club, FC
a liquid that trickled ran

explanation.surface: Money trickled into the city of Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liverpool' is the football club, so FC holds RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the money of France and is still used by Switzerland.

clue.text: Good time to have some, if unhappy?

indicators.note: having only some of the words means the letters sit within if unhappy

explanation.surface: A cheerful question: if you are unhappy, why not go and have a good time?
explanation.definitionFit: Fun is enjoyment, the amusement of a good time.

clue.text: Idiotic, a lapse in energy

parts.note: a moral lapse is a sin
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone calls a dip in energy idiotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like, so stupid or silly.

clue.text: Fair setter claiming foul, finally

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the setter word holds the letter

parts.note: cement is a thing that sets

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of foul

explanation.surface: A crossword setter finally claims a foul was committed, to be fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle's author but is something that sets: CEMENT, holding L.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild and pleasant, which is what fair weather is.

clue.text: Land report

definitions.meaning: a land or nation is a country
to report is to say or declare

explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a country, and to declare something is to say it formally.

clue.text: Integrate ductile ore

indicators.note: ductile metal can be drawn out and reshaped, so the letters are remoulded

explanation.surface: A recipe for building ductile ore into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ductile ore' looks like one definition; 'ductile' is the anagram signal on INTEGRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentite is silver sulphide, a mineral mined for silver.

clue.text: This number endlessly drink

indicators.note: endlessly removes the closing letter

parts.note: this clue is number 11, and a side of eleven players is a team

explanation.surface: An instruction to drink this number without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is 11 across; an eleven in football or cricket is a TEAM, which loses its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot infusion, Britain's favourite beverage.

clue.text: Elegant descent down onto joint

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
a dive is a seedy bar, as is a joint

explanation.surface: Someone gracefully descends onto a joint, perhaps tumbling into a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a graceful dive with arms spread like wings, entering the water elegantly.

clue.text: Look to protect journalist supporting joker in workers' movement

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means placed beneath

parts.note: a wag is a joker

indicators.note: the look wraps round the journalist to protect him

parts.note: a glance is a quick look
ED, an editor, is the stock journalist

explanation.surface: A trade union march: a joker backs a journalist under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' movement' looks like a trade union march; the workers are bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeybee workers perform this dance to tell the hive where food lies.

clue.text: One left to plug author, right away one's bored

indicators.note: plugging fills a gap, so these letters go inside
away means the letter is removed

parts.note: George Orwell, the author of Animal Farm
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A dull author is plugged by someone, a bored left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: ORWELL loses R to give OWELL; IL goes in after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft for petroleum is made by drilling, so it is something bored into the ground.

clue.text: Increase in staff replacing us in a month

indicators.note: replacing means the staff word takes the place of us

parts.note: August is a month
staff are the men employed

explanation.surface: A rise in staff numbers in a summer month means fewer of us.
explanation.walkthrough: In AUGUST, the US is swapped for MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to make larger or add to, a synonym of increase.

clue.text: Doctor resigns as a way of introduction

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A GP quits by way of introduction to a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject, but is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or means of entering, a way in.

clue.text: Ground on fire around bottom of garden, a flaming nightmare!

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the single letter
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reworked
in a down entry, the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A burning garden: the ground is on fire, a nightmare for its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reworks ON FIRE into INFERO, round N from 'garden'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging blaze, hellishly hot and terrifying.

clue.text: Book, for example, upset rival, not me!

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: not means the letters are left out

parts.note: a nemesis is an arch-rival

explanation.surface: A book upsets a rival, who protests it isn't about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EG into GE; NEMESIS without ME leaves NESIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The first book of the Bible, telling of creation.

clue.text: Top waves on one

parts.note: surf is breaking waves
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A top surfer is riding the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface is the uppermost layer of anything.

clue.text: Gentle exercise courses involving a minimum of intensity

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the courses word holds the letter

parts.note: the courses of a meal come on plates

indicators.note: a minimum is the least possible, so just the first letter of intensity

explanation.surface: Fitness classes offering gentle exercise involve little intensity.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a low-impact workout for core strength and posture.

clue.text: Bone in halibut's tail spoiling Spanish dish

indicators.note: spoiling means getting into and ruining the dish, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: tail picks the last letter of the fish

explanation.surface: A cook finds a bone in the halibut's tail, ruining the paella.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the tail of 'halibut', goes into PAELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a small bone at the front of the knee.

clue.text: Arbiter consumed by work in plant

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed, so the official goes inside

parts.note: toil is hard work
a ref, or referee, is the arbiter in a match

explanation.surface: A referee is consumed by his work at a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory; it is a botanical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is clover and similar plants with three-part leaves.

clue.text: Happen to wear fleece as a furry female!

indicators.note: the fleece word is worn around the other letters

parts.note: to shear a sheep is to take its fleece
to be is to happen or occur, as in 'what will be'

explanation.surface: A creature happens to wear fleece, as a furry female does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a garment, but means to shear.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult female of a bear species, covered in thick fur.

clue.text: House of iron valued with windows

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a nest houses birds
rated means valued

explanation.surface: An iron house, highly valued, with windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenestrated comes from Latin fenestra, a window, so it means having openings.

clue.text: Sheepish female solver on the phone?

indicators.note: heard over the phone means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the solver is you, the person doing the puzzle

explanation.surface: A sheepish woman rings the puzzle solver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like embarrassed but means ovine.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, so literally a female of sheep kind.

clue.text: Out of practice, one getting hammered? That's whisky and Drambuie!

parts.note: rusty means out of practice
a nail is driven in by a hammer

explanation.surface: A rusty drinker getting hammered on whisky and Drambuie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammered' looks like drunk but means struck with a hammer. Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of Scotch with Drambuie, served over ice.

clue.text: Salt Lake City all ends up, still

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read bottom to top
all ends takes the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: Every road in Salt Lake City ends uphill, still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all ends' gives TEY; 'up' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet and still are synonyms meaning even so or nevertheless.

clue.text: High time expanded, initially, ghost town population

parts.note: high noon is midday, the time of high sun

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of expanded

explanation.surface: High noon, the expanded scene in a deserted Western town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High time' suggests about time, but means noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost town is deserted, so nobody lives there.

clue.text: Cricket side ready for attack

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
set means ready

explanation.surface: A cricket team ready to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of an assault, an attack or start.

clue.text: Always carrying brand on both sides of label, one putting on a coat

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so these letters go inside

parts.note: e'er is the poetic form of ever, always

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, so the brand comes first with the label's sides beside it

parts.note: a brand is a name

indicators.note: both sides gives the first and last letters of label

explanation.surface: A brand carried on a label for someone putting on a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Always' is the poetic contraction e'er; 'a coat' is paint or glaze, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: One who applies enamel, a glossy coating, to pottery or metal.
